output.summary: Accra online revenue surged 148% from May to July 2026, driven by a 96% ad spend increase. Revenue grew from ₦1.48M to ₦3.68M, a ₦2.19M increase concentrated entirely in the online channel [H2]. Total ad spend rose 96% to ₦4.26M, with Meta spend up 204% to ₦3.04M, aligning with the revenue jump [H1]. Growth was led by CHIN-250 (+₦688K), PUFF-6PK (+₦430K), and PLNT-150 (+₦408K) [H6]. Stockouts, price changes, and normal seasonality were ruled out as causes [H7][H8][H9].

brief.headline: Accra online revenue surged 148% from May to July 2026, driven by a 96% ad spend increase.
brief.summary: Revenue grew from ₦1.48M to ₦3.68M, a ₦2.19M increase concentrated entirely in the online channel [H2]. Total ad spend rose 96% to ₦4.26M, with Meta spend up 204% to ₦3.04M, aligning with the revenue jump [H1]. Growth was led by CHIN-250 (+₦688K), PUFF-6PK (+₦430K), and PLNT-150 (+₦408K) [H6]. Stockouts, price changes, and normal seasonality were ruled out as causes [H7][H8][H9].

causes.statement: Increased ad spend on Meta and Google in Accra drove higher online traffic and conversions.
causes.finding: Total Accra ad spend rose 96.0% from ₦2.17M (May) to ₦4.26M (July). Meta spend surged 203.9% (₦1.00M→₦3.04M), Google +3.4% (₦531K→₦550K), radio +7.5% (₦422K→₦453K), billboard flat (-0.4%). The large Meta increase aligns with the 148% online revenue growth. Follow-up evidence q_ae30466deafe5be7 reviewed (4 rows).

evidence.sql: SELECT platform, SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-07' THEN spend_ngn ELSE 0 END) AS target, SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-05' THEN spend_ngn ELSE 0 END) AS baseline FROM kola.ad_platform WHERE city = 'Accra' AND month IN ('2026-05', '2026-07') GROUP BY platform ORDER BY platform

SELECT platform, SUM(spend_ngn) AS total_spend_ngn, SUM(impressions) AS total_impressions, SUM(clicks) AS total_clicks, SUM(spend_ngn)/NULLIF(SUM(clicks),0) AS cpc_ngn FROM kola.ad_platform WHERE city='Accra' AND month IN ('2026-05','2026-06','2026-07') GROUP BY platform ORDER BY total_spend_ngn DESC

causes.statement: Most of the change sits in the online channel
causes.finding: The change is concentrated in: online ₦2.19M (100% of the net change).

evidence.sql: SELECT channel, SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-07' THEN revenue_ngn ELSE 0 END) AS target, SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-05' THEN revenue_ngn ELSE 0 END) AS baseline FROM kola.erp_sales WHERE month IN ('2026-05', '2026-07') AND city = 'Accra' GROUP BY channel ORDER BY channel

causes.statement: Most of the change sits in Chin-Chin 250g (CHIN-250) and Puff-Puff Mix 6-pack (PUFF-6PK) and Plantain Chips 150g (PLNT-150)
causes.finding: The change is concentrated in: Chin-Chin 250g (CHIN-250) ₦687.6k (31% of the net change); Puff-Puff Mix 6-pack (PUFF-6PK) ₦430.0k (20% of the net change); Plantain Chips 150g (PLNT-150) ₦407.7k (19% of the net change).

evidence.sql: SELECT sku, SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-07' THEN revenue_ngn ELSE 0 END) AS target, SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-05' THEN revenue_ngn ELSE 0 END) AS baseline FROM kola.erp_sales WHERE month IN ('2026-05', '2026-07') AND city = 'Accra' AND channel = 'online' GROUP BY sku ORDER BY SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-07' THEN revenue_ngn ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-05' THEN revenue_ngn ELSE 0 END)

ruled_out.statement: Warehouse stockouts in Accra cut what could be sold
ruled_out.finding: Accra warehouse stockouts did not increase between May and July 2026. Only GROU-200 had 1 stockout day in July (vs 0 in May); all other SKUs had 0 stockout days in both months. This minimal stockout change cannot explain the +148% revenue growth (₦1.48M → ₦3.68M).

evidence.sql: SELECT sku, SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-07' THEN stockout_days ELSE 0 END) AS target, SUM(CASE WHEN month = '2026-05' THEN stockout_days ELSE 0 END) AS baseline FROM kola.warehouse_inventory WHERE city = 'Accra' AND month IN ('2026-05', '2026-07') GROUP BY sku ORDER BY sku

ruled_out.statement: A list price change moved demand
ruled_out.finding: No list price changes occurred for Accra between May and July 2026. The price_book query returned zero rows for effective_date > '2026-05-01' AND effective_date <= '2026-07-31' AND city IN ('Accra', 'ALL'), meaning no price changes were recorded during the period when revenue grew 148% (₦1.48M → ₦3.68M). The context table showing SKU targets vs baselines appears unrelated to the hypothesis period.

evidence.sql: SELECT effective_date, sku, city, old_price_ngn, new_price_ngn, reason FROM kola.price_book WHERE effective_date > '2026-05-01' AND effective_date <= '2026-07-31' AND city IN ('Accra', 'ALL') ORDER BY effective_date

ruled_out.statement: This is the normal seasonal pattern for these months
ruled_out.finding: A year earlier the same months moved +4.4% (₦1.29M → ₦1.35M), against +148.0% now (₦1.48M → ₦3.68M): this is not the normal seasonal pattern.

evidence.sql: SELECT month, SUM(revenue_ngn) AS value FROM kola.erp_sales WHERE month IN ('2025-05', '2025-07') AND city = 'Accra' AND channel = 'online' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

unresolved.statement: A new product launch or promotional campaign specifically for Accra online boosted SKU-level sales.
unresolved.finding: All six Accra online SKUs grew units strongly from May to July 2026 (CHIN-250: 387→960, PLNT-150: 304→757, GROU-200: 192→469, COCO-100: 176→449, KOKO-500: 133→321, PUFF-6PK: 113→285). Revenue rose from ₦1.48M to ₦3.68M (+148%). The broad-based lift across every SKU is consistent with a general demand surge or marketing push, but the rows do not identify a specific new product launch or Accra-only promotional campaign. No launch dates, campaign tags, or SKU-level price changes are present.

unresolved.statement: Improved delivery reliability or speed for Accra online orders increased customer retention and repeat purchases.
unresolved.finding: Model and numbers disagree. Model: Accra online logistics worsened from May to July 2026: late-delivery rate rose from 6.0% (29/485) to 7.2% (37/516) and average delay increased from 4.1 to 4.4 hours. This contradicts the hypothesis that improved delivery reliability or speed drove the 148% revenue growth.. Numbers: Deliveries moved somewhat (late-delivery rate 6.0%→7.2%, avg delay up to 4.4h), too little to be the main cause.

unresolved.statement: Competitor exit or reduced competition in Accra online market captured additional demand for our products.
unresolved.finding: The evidence shows price complaints in Accra rose from 30 (May) to 40 (July), which does not indicate a competitor exit or reduced competition. A competitor exit would typically reduce price pressure and complaints, not increase them. No data on competitor presence, market share, or competitive actions is provided.

caveats: Kòlá Foods is a fictional company; its systems hold synthetic demo data.
The size of [H1]'s effect cannot be measured directly from these systems; it is supported by direction and timing, not by a measured share.

recommendations: Keep the ad mix that moved results in Accra and measure its return per platform before scaling.
